question: Can a recursive Streeling improvement claim be tested against distinct drafting, human review, publication, and public-readback stages rather than draft counts alone?
production_path: investigation: inspect pinned review-candidate snapshot and progress reporter without treating triage as approval
model: separate review and publication queues with bounded weekly capacities
simulation: compare flat and growing accepted-review capacity under fixed publication capacity
adversarial: check queue conservation and identify the moved bottleneck
test: deterministic fixture rerun and five answered, falsifiable reasoning exercises
hypothesis: Improving an upstream stage will not increase verified public-course throughput when a downstream gate remains fixed; recursive improvement must measure the complete path and quality guardrails.
evidence: Demerzel source snapshot 3d175ab88b06f6fd06cfa8475b3f7e9be6323a6b records 21 course directories, 113 core course codes, 114 English drafts, nine six-locale/five-answer triage candidates, four committed review briefs, and zero approved production-review flags. These source signals are not authenticated human review or publication.

At fixture commit 4d322fbc8d6d12a111616558c9a503a1193c80ab, synthetic flat capacities yield 16 accepted, 16 published, and 32 waiting review after four weeks. Growing accepted-review capacity under fixed publication capacity yields 48 accepted, 16 published, and 32 waiting publication. The simulation assumes every review approves and all approved items can be published.

The simulator rerun produced byte-identical JSON, and both scenarios satisfy new-ready = accepted + waiting-review and accepted = published + waiting-publication. These are arithmetic checks, not a measured operational intervention.

PSY-003 has five answered exercises that distinguish source counts, hypothetical queue arithmetic, quality guardrails, and a falsifier. No human subject review, learner task result, translation, or public readback exists for this course; research duration was not instrumented and duration_seconds=0 records that limitation.
